purpose: Measure whether pinned host input changes the upload and the complete call of the three existing CUDA workloads, against pageable input in the same process, with the card's link at PCIe generation 4 and 16 lanes, so the result can be set beside the run of 2026-11-25 at generation 3

repeats.protocol: docs/pinned-protocol.json as amended in 982ce814103e56e9749eb145e9ce35f5c3e03a0c, whose one run on 2026-11-25 read the link as PCIe generation 3 with 16 lanes, current and maximum, after the run
repeats.reason: the motherboard's setting for the card's slot held the link at generation 3 until the evening of 2026-11-25, which halves the link's peak bandwidth for the copies this comparison exists to measure. It now allows generation 4, and nvidia-smi read the maximum as generation 4 with 16 lanes on 2026-11-26
changes: the link generation and width are part of the protocol, at generation 4 and 16 lanes
tools/run_pinned.py reads the link with nvidia-smi every 250 milliseconds while the benchmark runs and keeps every reading in the receipt
the samples and the receipt are named pinned-gen4.csv and pinned-gen4-execution.json, so the run of 2026-11-25 stays as it is
repeats.unchanged: the benchmark, the plan, the run order, the samples per condition, the GPU readings, the timing boundaries, the correctness checks and the limits are those of docs/pinned-protocol.json, and tools/run_pinned.py refuses to run if they differ. The summary keeps every entry of that protocol and adds the link readings and the comparison with the run of 2026-11-25

pcie_link.readings: tools/run_pinned.py starts nvidia-smi right before the benchmark and stops it once the benchmark exits, and keeps every reading in the receipt. An idle card drops its link to generation 1 to save power, so readings at generation 1 during the start, the idle pauses and the end are expected and kept
pcie_link.qualifies: the run is passed only when the readings exist, every one gives the maximum as generation 4 with 16 lanes, every one gives the current link either as generation 4 with 16 lanes or as the idle generation 1, and at least one gives it as generation 4 with 16 lanes. A reading at generation 2 or 3, or at generation 4 with fewer lanes, would mean the link trained down while the benchmark ran, and the run is then unqualified and kept
pcie_link.side_effect: the nvidia-smi process runs beside every timed row, which the run of 2026-11-25 did not have, so a comparison of the two runs carries that difference too

preconditions: source and protocol committed before collection
native and CUDA correctness passed on the measuring computer
no game running, checked privately by the person who starts the run, while the usual desktop applications keep using the GPU and their load is recorded with every sample
no other build, benchmark or GPU job of this computer's lanes running, which heavy.lock records
nvidia-smi gives the link maximum as generation 4 with 16 lanes before the run
histogram_bins: shared block bins, the default of cuda_tile_histogram
inputs: values i modulo 1009 divided by 1009 minus 0.5, mask true unless i is a multiple of 3, image byte i times 13 modulo 256
pinned_input: cudaMallocHost buffers filled from the pageable vectors and compared byte for byte with them before any run row
output: unchanged, every call downloads into host memory the runtime owns, a vector for the histogram and the stencil and a local double for the reduction, so the download is pageable for both kinds and serves as a control
first_sample: iteration zero is one of the 121 retained rows of each condition, reported apart from the 120 warm samples that the summary uses, and it is not a cold process measurement
order: for iteration k and side index c, run position p from 0 to 5 holds workload (k+c+floor(p/2)) modulo three and host memory (p+k) modulo two, with pageable as memory 0. Each workload thus runs with pageable and pinned input back to back, pageable first in even iterations and pinned first in odd ones, and over any six iterations each workload holds each place in the round with each memory kind first exactly once. Two additional warmup rounds follow iteration zero
pairs: the pageable row and the pinned row of one side, workload and iteration form a pair, and the ratio of their complete calls is taken within the pair, so that both calls share nearly the same background load
gpu_readings: before each recorded row, outside host timing, hbr_cuda_pinned_bench reads the card through NVML, which it opens at run time from System32 on Windows and finds by the UUID of the CUDA device. gpu_util_percent is the percent of the last NVML sample period, between 1/6 and 1 second, in which any kernel of any process ran, so it includes kernels of this benchmark's earlier calls as well as the desktop's. gpu_memory_mib is the memory all processes hold on the card, this benchmark included. Before each side and after the last one, a pause of 2 seconds with no call from this process precedes an idle reading, printed to stderr and kept in the receipt. Its utilization shows the desktop load alone, while its memory still includes this process, whose CUDA context and NVML session stay open for the whole run. The GPU UUID is not printed
context: device discovery and cudaFree(nullptr) create the primary context before any recorded row
setup_and_retirement: per side, one setup row times the three cudaMallocHost calls and one retire row times the three cudaFreeHost calls, both outside every run row
host_timing: steady_clock entry through return of an owned completed result, which includes validation, host result allocation, H2D, kernels, D2H, synchronization and the simple call's resource cleanup
outside_host_timing: the NVML readings and idle pauses
device_timing: same stream upload, kernel and download events, not summed with host elapsed time
correctness: every recorded and warmup output compared with the scalar CPU reference, exact for histogram counts, 1e-9 for the reduction and 1e-12 per stencil value, and every reduction and stencil output equal bit for bit to the first output of its workload and side across both memory kinds
summary: median and quartiles of the 120 paired pinned to pageable ratios of the complete call for each side and workload, and their medians with pageable first and with pinned first
median and range of gpu_util_percent and gpu_memory_mib for each side, and the idle readings
the link readings counted by current generation and width
for each side, workload and memory kind, the median complete call and median upload at generation 3 and at generation 4 beside each other
scope: pinned input only, through the unchanged runtime interface, with no pinned output, transfer overlap, multiple streams, zero copy, device resident input or Python
environment: record CPU, GPU, driver, CUDA toolkit compiler, host compiler, OS, source, protocol and binary identities, GPU utilization, memory and temperature before and after, and the link readings in the receipt that tools/run_pinned.py writes, have the person who starts the run check the GPU processes beforehand for a game, confirm with --confirm-desktop-load that none runs and keep that list in a private record outside the repository, since the computer is a shared desktop, and preserve ordinary applications and default settings
decision: retain slower and neutral results and report the pinned and pageable medians side by side for each condition without a general bandwidth claim. Set each condition beside the run of 2026-11-25 with both link generations named, and claim no cause for a difference between the two runs, since they ran on different days at different desktop loads, one run each. Label every published result as measured on a working desktop, with the load the readings show stated beside it
historical_evidence: leave the run of 2026-11-25 at generation 3, its samples, receipt, protocol and results page, the 504 original rows, the 900 reuse rows, their protocols and the cost model unchanged
